title: Upload → reconstruction (self-host/bridge, ADR-0005) → splat + collision mesh stored
summary: Wire the upload bundle to the reconstruction backend chosen in ADR-0005 (the self-hosted Gaussian-splat pipeline, or a managed bridge — Autodesk APS / KIRI-under-terms — during early validation) through the Inngest pipeline: submit the job, poll, store the Gaussian splat and collision mesh in staging storage behind signed URLs, track per-job cost, and halt at the daily cap. Backend and its terms come from the M1-CAPT-03 spike.

acceptance_tests.test: A capture bundle submitted through the pipeline returns a stored Gaussian splat and a collision mesh in staging, retrievable only through a signed, short-lived URL.
acceptance_tests.evidence: pipeline run log + storage listing (no secrets)

acceptance_tests.test: Per-job cost (GPU or bridge API) is recorded; the pipeline halts new jobs at the $50/day cap and resumes the next day.

If a managed bridge is used, its terms (written no-train + DPA + data residency) are on file in legal/vendors/ before any user (non-corpus) scan is sent (AUTH #030); absent that commitment there is no bridge and self-host is the sole path. The self-host path keeps scan media on our own infra. Corpus scans are Owner-supplied and consented.
No reconstruction backend key, GPU credential, or storage credential appears in the repo; secrets live only in .env.local / CI.

Ten corpus rooms reconstruct end to end; failure modes are logged with the input that caused them, including the on-device readiness score and coverage map; a downstream failure returns the kind free-retry handoff (SPEC §3.1, AUTH #025).
